title: Geometric stalk of Zariski-to-etale module pullback
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $\epsilon_T:(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}})\to(T_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_T)$ be the canonical morphism of ringed sites, with tensor module pullback and restriction direct image [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. Let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] with image $x$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{T,x}$ and let $K\subseteq\Omega$ be the separable algebraic closure of the residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] in $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure]. Write $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the strict henselization of the local ring $R$ relative to $K$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization]. Geometric stalks mean the pointed-etale-neighbourhood colimits [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; Zariski module stalks are [def-pc-module-stalk-functor]. There is a canonical $R$-algebra isomorphism
$$\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et},\bar x}\cong R^{\mathrm{sh}}.$$
For every sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal O_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], without any quasi-coherence hypothesis, there is a natural isomorphism of $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-modules
$$(\epsilon_T^*M)_{\bar x}\cong M_x\otimes_R R^{\mathrm{sh}}.$$
The ring map used on the right is the structural map of the strict henselization, and the isomorphisms commute with every module morphism $M\to N$.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring; sites-modules.tex Tag 05V5, lemma-pullback-stalk, applied to epsilon_T and its geometric point; combined in spaces-perfect.tex proof of Tag 08H8, lemma-epsilon-flat.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ containing $x$, and let $\mathfrak p$ correspond to $x$. The affine-open stalk localization identifies $A_{\mathfrak p}$ with $R$, carrying $a/1$ to its germ. Compute the structure-ring stalk as the pointed-neighbourhood colimit. Restrict to affine neighbourhoods mapping into $U$: every neighbourhood admits such a refinement by applying the affine-shrink lemma to the inverse image of $U$. The pointed-neighbourhood category is cofiltered, so the full-subcategory colimit lemma applies. To stay within small indices, choose representatives from the set of affine etale schemes of the essential-smallness lemma, with each possible lift of $\bar x$; those lifts form a set of scheme morphisms. This is a small full subcategory and every affine pointed object is isomorphic to a representative. The same full-subcategory lemma therefore justifies the restriction to representatives. Thus the stalk is canonically the colimit of the rings $B$ for affine pointed etale $\operatorname{Spec}B\to U$. All identifications preserve restriction maps and the germs of elements of $A$.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, proof, affine neighbourhood and cofinal system.

proof.text: A lift $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ over $\bar x$ is exactly a prime $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p$ and a compatible embedding $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\Omega$, by the geometric-point description. The etale residue-field lemma makes every element of $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ separable algebraic over $\kappa(x)$, so this embedding has image in $K$ by its definition. Conversely an embedding into $K$ gives the lift by $K\subseteq\Omega$. These operations are inverse on objects; on arrows the affine spectrum correspondence identifies a pointed scheme map with an $A$-algebra map $B\to B'$ preserving the residue embedding. Hence the opposite affine-neighbourhood diagram is precisely the ring diagram of etale residue triples over $(A,\mathfrak p,K)$, not just a diagram with the same objects. The equivalence clause of the colimit lemma identifies their colimits with the same coprojections.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, proof, translation into triples and factorization through the separable closure.

proof.text: Apply the strict-henselization-triples lemma to the ring $A$, prime $\mathfrak p$, and separable closure $K$: the relative-separable-closure definition ensures that $K$ is indeed a separable closure because $\Omega$ is algebraically closed. Its canonical colimit identification gives $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et},\bar x}\cong(A_{\mathfrak p})^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Substitute the germ-preserving localization $A_{\mathfrak p}\cong R$ from step 1 to obtain $\alpha:\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et},\bar x}\cong R^{\mathrm{sh}}$. This is an $R$-algebra isomorphism: every $a\notin\mathfrak p$ becomes invertible already in the refinement $D(a)\subset U$, so the map out of $A$ on both sides extends uniquely to $A_{\mathfrak p}$; on $b/a$ it is the germ of $b$ times the inverse germ of $a$. Thus the induced scalar map is the structural strict-henselization map required in the statement.

source.place: Tag 04HX, lemma-describe-etale-local-ring, last sentence, applying algebra.tex Tag 04GW, lemma-strict-henselization-different.

proof.text: Let $p$ be the etale topos point whose inverse image is the geometric stalk, supplied by the geometric-stalk-topos-point lemma, and put $q=\epsilon_Tp$. For any set $E$ its direct image has, on a Zariski open $W$, the value $(q_*E)(W)=(p_*E)(W)=\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{Hom}_T(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,W),E)$, since $\epsilon_{T,*}$ is restriction. The Hom set is a singleton if $x\in W$ and empty otherwise, so this is exactly the ordinary skyscraper at $x$, including its restriction maps. Explicitly a morphism $F\to q_*E$ is a compatible family $F(W)\to E$ for opens $W\ni x$; by the defining colimit of germs this is a map $F_x\to E$. Thus its left adjoint $q^{-1}$ is canonically the ordinary stalk at $x$. The correspondence preserves addition, multiplication and scalar action because they are induced on germs. In particular the composition comparison identifies $(\epsilon_T^{-1}M)_p$ with $M_x$ and $(\epsilon_T^{-1}\mathcal O_T)_p$ with $R$.

source.place: Tag 08H8, lemma-epsilon-flat, proof: image of the geometric point on the Zariski site; explicit skyscraper calculation, using the point model of etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04FM.

proof.text: Apply the general ringed-topos tensor-pullback stalk comparison to $u=\epsilon_T$, the point $p$ of step 4, and the arbitrary $\mathcal O_T$-module $M$. Its hypotheses require only a morphism of ringed topoi and a module, both supplied here. It gives a natural isomorphism $(\epsilon_T^*M)_{\bar x}\cong M_x\otimes_R\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et},\bar x}$, using precisely the stalk of the structure map as its ring map. Compose with $1\otimes\alpha$ from step 3. The resulting comparison is $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-linear, with inverse obtained by $1\otimes\alpha^{-1}$ and the inverse pullback-stalk comparison. For a morphism $h:M\to N$, naturality of that comparison gives the tensor map $h_x\otimes1$; composing with the fixed $1\otimes\alpha$ preserves this equality. This proves the claimed naturality and both clauses, without any quasi-coherence assumption.
